column1: # *** THE UK NATIONAL ARCHIVES - DISCOVERY. Searched for the first time, 17 September 2026. ***
# David asked whether this archive had ever looked at nationalarchives.gov.uk. It had not: three
# mentions of 'National Archives' in the whole corpus and all three are nationalarchives.gov.ZA.
# *** Free, no login, no CAPTCHA *** - the JSON API at /API/search/records answers 200 unauthenticated,
# which clears both of the walls that stop CEMLA and the GRO.
# *** CONTROL: 'Bideford' returns 16,510 records ***, so every zero below is a tested zero.
# *** Discovery aggregates ~2,500 UK repositories, not just Kew *** - on the Bideford control,
# TNA held 4,791 and OTHER archives 11,719, most of them North Devon Record Office.

column3: FO 925/3930, a 1788 Seville street plan dedicated to Don Pedro Lopez de Lerena, a Spanish finance minister; and BT 400/3953/3, a 1915 crew list matching incidentally.
column4: *** A CLEAN TESTED NULL, AND THE FIRST ONE THIS SURNAME HAS HAD IN BRITAIN. *** Neither record is a person of this family. *** Llerena *** returns 1 (a Peninsular War letter about the Spanish town) and *** Lerina *** 2, both incidental. *** The surname is absent from UK archives ***, which is what you would expect of a family that went Rosario to the Cape without touching Britain.

column3: 347 at Kew, 292 elsewhere. Chancery suits from 1603, wills, and a dense run of North Devon Record Office deeds.
column4: *** THE ENGLISH SIDE IS RICHLY DOCUMENTED AND THIS ARCHIVE HAD NOT LOOKED. *** Mary Septima Taylor, who married Pablo Armando, was a Brayley on her mother's side - Mary Ann Hellen BRAYLEY, 1843-1900.

column3: Leases and releases naming *** George Brayley of Bideford, gent *** across 1769, 1831 and 1861; *** B194/277/1-5 ***, valuations and a list of leases of *** G.B. Brayley's property in Northam, Bideford and Barnstaple ***, 1915 and 1929.
column4: *** A BRAYLEY FAMILY OF STANDING IN BIDEFORD AND NORTHAM, 1767 TO 1861, IN DEEDS NOBODY HERE HAS OPENED. *** Whether they join Mary Ann Hellen Brayley is *** untested *** and is not assumed here.

column3: ADM 106/1153/18, 1767: timber from New England on the brig Cato, *** George Brayley master ***, at Appledore. 2239 B-8/41, 1827: *** George Brayley of Orchard Hill, parish of Northam, gent. ***
column4: Appledore is in Northam parish. *** A Brayley shipmaster in 1767 and a Brayley landowner at Orchard Hill in 1827. *** Recorded as context, not as ancestry.

column3: *** IR 26/337/185 ***, abstract of the will of *** George Brayley, Gentleman of Northam ***, 29 May 1800. *** B127-8/126/1-3 ***, probate copy will of *** Emily Kate Brayley of Northam ***, dated 1935, proved 1943. *** B127-8/139/1-12 ***, probate copy will of *** Edith Mary Brayley of Northam ***, dated 1943, proved 1948.
column4: *** WILLS NAME RELATIONSHIPS, WHICH IS EXACTLY WHAT THE BRAYLEY ASCENT IS SHORT OF. *** Three of them, two within living memory of Mary Septima. *** The highest-value thing this search turned up for the ascent. ***

column3: *** ADM 157/197/182 *** , folios 182-186: *** John Walker Brayley, born Middlesex ***, attestation papers for the Royal Marines, *** 1861, aged 18 ***, discharged 1868 as an Invalid - and *** joined from the SOUTH DEVON MILITIA. ***
column4: *** A CANDIDATE, AND IT LANDS ON AN OPEN DISCREPANCY. *** This archive has John Walker Brayley born *** 1845 at St Paul's, London *** - which IS Middlesex - and has already logged that his death index gives age 53 in Dec qtr 1900, implying *** about 1847, a two-year gap left open. *** Aged 18 in 1861 implies *** about 1843. *** Three sources, three different years, and a Royal Marines attestation states date and place of birth outright. *** And the militia line is the strongest thing here: *** a man born in Middlesex who was serving in a *** South Devon *** regiment is a Devon family's son born in London, which is exactly this family's shape. *** Still not asserted as him - order the document. ***

column3: Nothing. *** Control: 'Backway' alone returns 120 ***, so the term works and the engine handles two-word queries - 'John Walker Brayley' returned 4.
column4: *** A TESTED NULL FOR JOHN BACKWAY BRAYLEY. *** Recorded only because the control was run first.

column3: *** IT IS A SCHOOL. *** ED 70/427 (1909-1919) and ED 21/26168 (1921-1933), *** Bideford, Geneva Place Council School ***, at Kew; and *** 629C at North Devon Record Office, log books and ADMISSION REGISTERS, 1885-1949. ***
column4: *** THIS REOPENS ROW 123, WHICH I CLOSED THIS MORNING AS 'NOT TESTABLE FREE'. *** That verdict tested the census route only and never asked whether a catalogue held the street. *** School admission registers name the child, the date of birth, the father and THE ADDRESS *** - and Lucy Elizabeth (b.1881), Mary Septima (b.1884) and Agnes Walker (b.1889) were all of school age inside 1885-1949. *** It does not confirm 23 Geneva Place for Horace, born 1872 and too old for these registers. *** It gives the address question a route it did not have.

column3: Every hit is a document that merely contains the words - crew lists, a Metropolitan Police leavers' register, an 18th-century division list.
column4: *** THE LIMIT OF THIS SOURCE, AND IT MATTERS MORE THAN ANY SINGLE HIT. *** Discovery does *** not *** name-index ordinary civilians. It indexes people only where a SERIES was catalogued name by name - ADM 157 and ADM 188 for the services, PROB and IR 26 for wills, ADM 73, AIR 76 and AIR 79. *** Searching a civilian's full name here will return noise and must never be written down as a null about that person. *** The Brayley results above are catalogue entries for deeds and wills, not a family index.
